Consult Summary:
- Young woman with 3-day history of sudden-onset, severe generalized headache (worse over right eye) with photophobia and intermittent visual "shooting lights"; partial analgesic response. Clinician suspects migraine but plans urgent face-to-face neurological exam and fundoscopy to exclude secondary causes (DDx supports migraine as most likely; CVST and IIH are considered).

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - "Blinding" headache for 3 days, started suddenly on waking; continuous with fluctuant intensity.
  - Pain described as generalized but stronger over the right eye.
  - Severity reported as 8/10 at worst, reducing to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
  - Photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena described as "shooting lights" or "weird kind of vision."
  - Feels "a bit sick" but no vomiting.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: woke with headache 3 days ago.
  - Course: persistent every day since onset; partial transient relief with ibuprofen; patient stayed home 1 full day, attempted limited work on other days.
  - Sleep: able to sleep; headache does not wake her from sleep but may be present on waking.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Partially relieved by ibuprofen (not fully).
  - Paracetamol suggested by clinician as additional analgesic.
  - Occasional stabbing pain when standing up quickly or moving head.
  - Photophobia worsens symptoms.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No vomiting (patient denies), no fever reported, no cough, no nasal or sinus symptoms.
  - No numbness, tingling, or weakness.
  - No change in smell or taste.
  - No head trauma, no recent travel.
  - No morning vomiting or nocturnal wakening from headache.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No neck stiffness reported.
  - No visual loss per patient; recent eye check reportedly "nothing changed" in vision.
  - No seizures, no focal neurological deficits described.

Past Medical History:
- Headache history:
  - Occasional prior headaches in youth; previously short-lived (up to 2 days) and responsive to ibuprofen.
- Other medical conditions: none reported.
- Allergies: patient states none.
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill started ~1 year ago (type/name not documented).
  - Intermittent ibuprofen for headaches (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Paracetamol discussed to take concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other chronic medications documented.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Employment: works from home; recent headaches have reduced ability to work.
- Smoking: denies tobacco use.
- Alcohol: drinks alcohol approximately once weekly ("three, once a week" as reported) — frequency/quantity unclear.
- Recreational drug use: denies.

Family History:
- Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting).
- No other family history documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none recorded in transcript. Patient reports pharmacy BP check ~1 year ago was normal.
- Examination findings: no physical exam documented. Clinician plans neurological examination and fundoscopy at face-to-face appointment.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported.
- Clinician plan: arrange face-to-face neurological exam and fundoscopy; BP check at appointment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Integrate transcript impressions with DDx insights: Transcript and DDx align that primary migraine is the most likely diagnosis but secondary causes (CVST, IIH, SAH) warrant consideration given new, severe, persistent headache and OCP use. Physical exam (neuro and fundoscopic) is essential; urgent escalation if red flags or deterioration.

- Issue 1: Probable migraine (most likely diagnosis)
  - Assessment:
    - Clinical features consistent with migraine: severe unilateral-predominant pain, photophobia, visual phenomena, family history of migraine, partial response to analgesia.
  - Plan:
    - Prescribe stronger analgesic than ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) as discussed by clinician.
    - Prescribe/advise paracetamol concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented) — take with food per clinician instruction.
    - Book urgent face-to-face appointment for neurological examination and fundoscopy; if symptoms resolve before visit, appointment may be cancelled.
    - Advise symptomatic measures (avoidance of bright lights; rest) as currently used by patient.

- Issue 2: Need to exclude secondary causes (CVST, IIH, SAH considered)
  - Assessment:
    - DDx raises concern for CVST and IIH given combined oral contraceptive use, female sex, persistent headache with visual disturbance; SAH less likely but still a consideration with new sudden severe headache.
    - No focal deficits, neck stiffness, vomiting, or altered consciousness reported, lowering immediate likelihood of SAH/meningitis, but persistent severe headache warrants examination.
  - Plan:
    - Perform urgent neurological exam and fundoscopic exam at face-to-face visit to look for focal signs or papilledema.
    - Check blood pressure at appointment to assess OCP suitability (clinician stated will check BP).
    - If neurological exam or fundoscopy is abnormal, or if clinical course worsens (increasing severity, focal signs, persistent vomiting, decreased consciousness), escalate to urgent imaging (CT/CT venogram or MRI/MR venogram) and/or emergency department evaluation (patient advised to go to A&E if headache becomes unbearable or changes).
    - Documented patient instructions: attend A&E if symptoms deteriorate markedly prior to scheduled appointment.

- Issue 3: Review of combined oral contraceptive (OCP) suitability
  - Assessment:
    - Patient on combined OCP ~1 year; clinician highlighted that if patient has typical migraine with aura or recurrent migraine with focal features, OCP may need review/change.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current OCP for now.
    - Reassess OCP suitability after clinical assessment (neurological exam and history); consider changing contraception if migraine with aura or other contraindications identified.

- Other general plan items (supported by transcript):
  - Arrange face-to-face appointment via support team for full examination and BP check.
  - Provide prescription for stronger analgesia and paracetamol (specific medications/doses not documented in transcript).
  - Provide safety-netting: return/seek urgent care for worsening headache, new focal deficits, vomiting, altered consciousness, or other red-flag features.
  - If necessary after examination, consider referral to specialist (patient asked about referral; clinician indicated referral can follow face-to-face assessment).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- 1) Migraine (probable migraine with visual aura) — Likelihood: High
  - Reasoning: Photophobia, visual phenomena ("shooting lights"), severe headache interfering with function, partial response to ibuprofen, positive family history (mother with migraines). No fever or focal deficits.
- 2) Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Likelihood: Moderate
  - Reasoning: Young woman on combined OCP (prothrombotic risk) with subacute progressive severe headache and visual symptoms; positional/stabbing elements reported. No focal deficits or papilledema documented yet; requires exclusion if exam abnormal or symptoms progress.
- 3) Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — Likelihood: Moderate
  - Reasoning: Young woman with persistent headache and transient visual phenomena; OCP use is a possible associated factor. Fundoscopy and assessment for papilledema required to evaluate.

- Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) — Likelihood: Low
  - Reasoning: Sudden-onset severe headache compatible, but absence of vomiting, neck stiffness, loss of consciousness, or classic thunderclap description makes SAH less likely; still consider if clinical deterioration.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, temperature, respiratory rate) are not recorded.
  - Formal neurological examination and fundoscopy findings are not available.
  - No imaging or laboratory results available.
  - Exact names, doses, routes, and frequencies for prescribed stronger analgesic and paracetamol not documented.
  - Exact type/name of combined oral contraceptive not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified; DDx aligns with transcript. (No conflict noted.)
- Transcript quality:
  - Brief audio/volume issue at start; remainder of consultation audible and content clear.
